s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive respiratory illness with systemic symptoms and neurological involvement
salient_findings: Cough, subjective fever, and shortness of breath
Right upper lobe infiltrate on chest radiograph
Positive Blastomyces urine antigen and Histoplasmosis blood antigen
Development of right-sided ptosis and anisocoria
key_facts: 81-year-old man with initial symptoms of cough, subjective fever, and shortness of breath
Treated with azithromycin and levofloxacin for bronchitis
Symptoms progressed despite antibiotics
Medical history includes coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, stage 3 chronic kidney disease, and type 2 diabetes mellitus
Spent time at a Northern Minnesota cabin with minimal outdoor exposure
Previous missionary work in Colombia ended two years before admission
Vital signs: Temperature 38.6°C, Pulse 130 beats/min, Blood Pressure 114/61 mm Hg, Respiratory Rate 22 breaths/min, Oxygen Saturation 82%
Lung sounds were diminished in the right upper lobe with diffuse crackles in the right lung base
Leukocytosis: 15,000/mm³
Procalcitonin: 0.77 ng/mL
Positive Blastomyces urine antigen and Histoplasmosis blood antigen
Negative results for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Cryptococcus, Legionella, and influenza
Bronchoscopy findings: Moderate clear secretions with erythematous and edematous bronchial mucosa
Bronchoalveolar lavage: Spherical broadly based budding yeast on Grocott-Gomori methenamine silver stain

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive Histoplasmosis blood antigen and consistent clinical presentation

shortlist.label: Blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive Blastomyces urine antigen and symptoms consistent with blastomycosis

shortlist.label: Coccidioidomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and exposure history consistent with coccidioidomycosis

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Although antigen test was negative, clinical presentation and immunocompromised state keep it in consideration

shortlist.label: Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe respiratory illness and potential for opportunistic infection
